items.headline: Strait of Hormuz traffic slows as insurance premiums spike overnight
bullets: War-risk rates for VLCC passages jumped after overnight drone activity near Bandar Abbas; two majors paused new bookings pending guidance.
Energy desks mark a 2–4 day disruption premium into front-month crude; refined-product cracks already reflecting the scare.
Watch: whether USN escorts resume the informal corridor protocol used in 2024 — markets price that faster than diplomacy.

items.headline: Spot ETF inflows resume after three-session pause; basis remains orderly
bullets: Combined US spot BTC ETF flows flipped positive (~$420M) after a brief risk-off flush; CME basis stayed inside a normal carry band.
On-chain: exchange reserves flat-to-down; long-term holder supply still grinding higher — not a distribution tape.
Hard-money read: liquidity returned without leverage blowups. That is the healthy path.

items.headline: Bullion holds bid as real yields soften into FOMC blackout
bullets: COMEX gold firmed on softer 10y TIPS; ETF holdings edged higher for a second session.
Central-bank buying narrative intact — Asia physical premiums remain elevated vs London.
Metals desk note: silver lagging gold again; ratio still favors gold as the macro hedge of choice this week.

items.headline: Claims soft, payrolls revisions still the quiet story
bullets: Initial claims printed below consensus; continuing claims drift sideways — labor cooling, not cracking.
Prior-month payroll revisions remain the underappreciated signal for late-cycle softness.
Rates: curve still inverted on the belly; markets lean toward a patient Fed, not a panic cut.

items.headline: WTI range-bound; distillate inventories the real tell
bullets: Crude held $70–73 as geopolitics and soft demand cancel each other; product cracks doing the work.
Distillate draws in the Midwest remain firmer than seasonal norms — diesel, not gasoline, is the hinge.
If Hormuz risk fades by Friday, expect a give-back into the range midpoint.

items.headline: Open-source: satellite revisit cadence rises over key Persian Gulf terminals
bullets: Commercial SAR tasking density increased over loading berths and nearby islands over 48h — pattern consistent with contingency monitoring, not a one-off look.
No confirmed kinetic strikes on export infrastructure as of this brief; signal is readiness, not aftermath.
Treat social footage as unverified until geolocated against known terminals.
